task: Connect the two blue Cat5e cables from the old phone block to new keystone jacks, join them with a patch cord, then test the link

plan.job_title: Terminate two Cat5e cables to keystone jacks
tools_needed: Punch-down tool (a small hand tool that pushes wire into a terminal slot and trims the excess — ~$10 at any hardware store)
110-type keystone jack x2 (the small snap-in data socket the patch cord plugs into — must say 'Cat5e' or 'Cat6' on the pack)
Cat5e patch cord, any length (a short pre-made cable with RJ45 plugs on both ends)
Cable tester (a two-piece device, ~$15, that checks all 8 wires lit up in sequence)

steps.title: Photograph the existing punch-down wiring
steps.action: Before touching anything, take a clear close-up photo of each blue cable where it is currently punched down into the phone block (the black panel with the colored wire terminals). This is your reference if you need to undo anything.
do_not_touch: any other cables already terminated in the block
steps.stop_condition: If any terminal looks scorched, melted, or smells burnt, stop and contact a professional.
steps.evidence_required: Photo shows both blue cables' wire colors clearly visible in their current terminal slots.

steps.title: Un-punch the first blue cable from the block
steps.action: Use the small flat-head screwdriver to gently lever each wire out of its slot on the phone block for the FIRST blue cable only. Work one wire at a time so they don't tangle.
steps.evidence_required: Photo shows the first blue cable hanging free with all its inner wires visible and unattached to the block.
highlight_targets: phone block terminal slots for that cable

steps.title: Trim and strip the first cable end
steps.action: Cut the cable end back about 2 inches (5 cm) to get a fresh, undamaged section of wire. Then use the wire stripper to remove the outer jacket (the blue plastic sleeve) for about 1 inch (2.5 cm), exposing the 4 twisted pairs (8 thin wires) inside.
steps.evidence_required: Photo shows ~1 inch of jacket removed revealing the 4 twisted pairs, with no nicks or cuts on any thin wire.

steps.title: Seat wires into first keystone jack using T568B order
steps.action: Hold a keystone jack (the small snap-in socket) with its color-coded wire guide facing you. Place each thin wire into its matching colored slot following the T568B pattern printed on the jack — this is the standard order: white-orange, orange, white-green, blue, white-blue, green, white-brown, brown. Do NOT untwist the pairs more than 0.5 inch (1.3 cm) each.
steps.evidence_required: Photo shows all 8 wires seated in the jack slots with correct colors visible and no wire crossing out of its slot.
highlight_targets: 8 thin inner wires of first cable

steps.title: Punch down the first keystone jack
steps.action: Press each wire firmly into its slot using the punch-down tool (position the tool blade over the wire in the slot and push straight down until you hear/feel a click). The tool will trim the excess wire automatically.
steps.evidence_required: Photo shows all 8 wires punched flush into the jack slots with no loose wire ends sticking up.

steps.title: Repeat steps 2–5 for the second blue cable
steps.action: Un-punch the second blue cable from the phone block, trim and strip its end exactly as in steps 2–3, seat the wires into the second keystone jack using the same T568B color order, and punch them down.
steps.evidence_required: Photo shows both keystone jacks fully punched down with no loose wire ends on either jack.

steps.title: Mount both keystone jacks in a surface
steps.action: Snap each finished keystone jack into a keystone wall-plate or patch-panel faceplate (a plastic frame that holds the jack steady) by pressing it in until it clicks. Both jacks should sit side by side.
do_not_touch: all other cables in the enclosure
steps.evidence_required: Photo shows both jacks snapped flush into the faceplate with no gaps or tilting.

steps.title: Connect the two jacks with a patch cord
steps.action: Plug one end of the patch cord (the short pre-made cable with RJ45 rectangular plugs on both ends) into jack 1, and the other end into jack 2. Press each plug in until you hear a click.
steps.evidence_required: Photo shows the patch cord plugged into both jacks with both locking tabs visible and engaged.

steps.title: Test the link with a cable tester
steps.action: Plug the main unit of the cable tester into one jack and the remote unit into the other jack (or directly onto each end of the loop). Switch it on and watch the indicator lights — all 8 lights (numbered 1–8) must flash in sequence with no skipped or lit-solid lights, which would mean a wiring fault.
steps.stop_condition: If any light is missing, stays on permanently, or the tester shows 'FAIL', do not use the link — recheck the wire color order in both jacks against the T568B label and re-punch if needed.
steps.evidence_required: Photo or video shows all 8 numbered lights on the tester cycling 1 through 8 in order with no gaps or errors.

0.reason: The photo does not show the blue cables punched down into a black phone block with wire colors clearly visible in their terminal slots — the wiring appears loose/pulled out and no close-up of the punch-down block terminals is visible.
